analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour + Wise / Man / MSFT pre 16 Oct 2026
key_insights: US equities rallied off morning lows to close Thursday in the green: SPX +33bps to 7744, NDX -5bps to 29,935, RTY +138bps to 2767. 8 of 11 sectors rose (Healthcare +1.84%, Materials +1.71%), Energy -1.55% and Tech -0.54% lagged.
AI headlines and debates continued to dominate risk appetite while defensive areas of the market caught a bid. Global Neoclouds (GSXGNEOC) rose 57bps after being down about 10% intraday.
Europe was constructive (SXXP +40bps, SX5E -40bps) on a rotation into Defensives (GSXEDEFS +2.5%) and Quality (GSPEQUAL +60bps).

Market breadth is weak under the index: 84% of SPX stocks trade at least 10% below their all-time highs (Real Estate 97%, Materials 96%, Utilities 94%). 10 stocks have driven 70% of the SPX return since end of Q1, and the other 490 stocks account for 30%.

GS US high-touch desk saw an uptick in long-only activity, with an early wave of semis supply around the open that slowed through the session. There was a flight-to-safety bid in pockets of Mag7, Staples, MedTech & Tools and Financials. The mid-day drift higher reflected less tech supply and broadening, with RTY > SPX > NDX. The desk saw no meaningful defense of AI or peripheral pockets.

Global AI positioning has come down from the June peak: net allocation is 26.1% of global single stock net market value (peak 31.7% in early June), and the aggregate long/short ratio is 3.27 (peak 4.34).

Hedge funds lost money Thursday: Global Fundamental L/S -0.5%, Global Systematic L/S -1.4% (-3.7 SD, worst day since Aug 19), Multi-Strats equity portfolio -1.2%. YTD, fundamental L/S is up 10% and systematic L/S is up 20%.

Fed: Kevin Warsh said that in the intermeeting period the world has broadly conformed to the Fed's September expectations. GS reads this, with other FOMC comments, as a pause in October, and still expects a second and final hike in December.

Schneider Electric reported a 3% sales beat with 17% organic growth, 300bps above consensus. EM and IA both beat, data center demand was up triple digits again, and 2026 EPS consensus is likely to rise by a low-single-digit percentage. GS reads the results favourably for ABB, Legrand and Siemens.
Schneider raised guidance to 12-14% organic growth (from 10-13%, consensus 13.3%, GS 14.6%) and margin to 19.7-19.9% (from 19.4-19.7%, consensus/GS 19.7%).

Memory: GS says CXMT's 4F2 announcement narrows the capacity gap, but a significant technology gap remains in advanced-node DRAM and HBM, which GS sees as supportive for Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

Wise delivered 2QFY27 transaction revenue growth of about 21% y/y ex-FX and net revenue growth of about 20%, modestly ahead of expectations. FY27 net revenue guidance moved to the upper half of the 15-20% medium-term range (17.5-20%). GS raised its FY27 net revenue growth estimate to 19.7% from 17.9% and cut its FY27 IBT margin estimate to 25.0% from 26.2% on higher one-offs and investment.

Man Group reported record 3Q26 AuM of $270.9bn, 4% ahead of GSe and Visible Alpha consensus. Net inflows were $10.1bn versus company-compiled consensus of $3.8bn, equal to 16% annualised organic growth.

Microsoft preview: GS rates MSFT Buy, on its Conviction List, with a $640 price target (20% upside), and calls it the best-positioned Software name for AI product cycles. For 1QFY, GS sees an upside case of Azure growth of 46-47% cc (guidance 44-45% cc) and a 2QFY guide of about 46-47% cc, with M365 Commercial Cloud growth of about 17-18% cc (guidance 17% cc).
NDX forward P/E is back to about 21x, the lowest since the AI cycle began in 2023, and the index has recaptured its 50- and 100-day moving averages.

Wise's FY27 net revenue growth estimate rose to 19.7% from 17.9%, while the IBT margin estimate fell to 25.0% from 26.2%.

sector_views.rationale: Europe saw a rotation into Defensives (GSXEDEFS +2.5%) and Quality, and US Healthcare (+1.84%) led while the high-touch desk saw a flight-to-safety bid in Staples and MedTech & Tools.
Schneider's beat and guidance raise read favourably for ABB, Legrand and Siemens on data center demand.

earnings_insights: Schneider Electric (reported 10/16): sales beat consensus by 3%, organic growth 17% (300bps above consensus). Guidance raised to 12-14% organic growth (consensus 13.3%, GS 14.6%) and margin 19.7-19.9% (consensus/GS 19.7%). GS says 2026 EPS consensus likely moves up by a low-single-digit percentage.

Wise (reported 2QFY27): transaction revenue growth about 21% y/y ex-FX, net revenue growth about 20%, modestly ahead of expectations. FY27 net revenue guidance is the upper half of the 15-20% range (17.5-20%). GSe FY27 net revenue growth 19.7% (from 17.9%), FY27 IBT margin 25.0% (from 26.2%).

Man Group (3Q26 AuM statement): record period-end AuM of $270.9bn, 4% ahead of GSe and Visible Alpha consensus and 3% ahead of company-compiled consensus. Net inflows of $10.1bn versus company-compiled consensus of $3.8bn.

Microsoft 1QFY preview (not yet reported): GS upside case is Azure growth of 46-47% cc versus 44-45% cc company guidance, a 2QFY guide of about 46-47% cc, and M365 Commercial Cloud growth of about 17-18% cc versus 17% cc guidance.
